title: Derived transport of represented left exact functors through injective comparisons
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories with enough injectives [def-sp-abelian, def-sp-enough-injectives], using derived categories in fixed compatible Hom universes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. Let $L:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be an additive exact functor, $P\in\mathcal A$, $P'\in\mathcal B$, and $d:LP\xrightarrow{\sim}P'$ an isomorphism. Let $S:\mathcal A\to\mathrm{Ab}$ and $S':\mathcal B\to\mathrm{Ab}$ be additive left exact functors [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Suppose given additive natural isomorphisms $\theta:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(P,-)\xrightarrow{\sim}S$ and $\theta':\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(P',-)\xrightarrow{\sim}S'$, and a natural transformation $\lambda:S\to S'\circ L$, satisfying, for every $M$ and $f:P\to M$,
$$\theta'_{LM}(Lf\circ d^{-1})=\lambda_M\theta_M(f).$$
Let $DL$ be termwise exact derived inverse image (with its termwise shift comparison). Write $b:RS\to RS'\circ DL$ for the canonical bounded-below right-derived comparison, namely the unique factorization of the termwise $\lambda$ followed by the target derived unit through the source derived unit [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective]. Let $\chi,\chi'$ be the isomorphisms from $H^a(RS(-))$, respectively $H^a(RS'(-))$, to morphisms from $P[0]$, respectively $P'[0]$, obtained by deriving $\theta^{-1},(\theta')^{-1}$ and using the roof-normalized comparison of [lem-sc-p1-rhom-hom-derived-roof].

For bounded-below complexes $F$, choose bounded-below degreewise injective resolutions $e:F\to I$ and $e':LF\to J$. There exists a chain map $t:LI\to J$ with $t\circ Le\simeq e'$, unique up to homotopy. In the injective models the canonical $b_F$ is represented by
$$S(I)\xrightarrow{\lambda_I}S'(LI)\xrightarrow{S'(t)}S'(J).$$
For every cocycle $f:P\to I^a$, its image under this map corresponds through $\theta'$ to the cocycle $t^a\circ Lf\circ d^{-1}:P'\to J^a$. Consequently for every $a\in\mathbf Z$ and $\alpha\in H^a(RS(F))$,
$$\chi'_{DLF}\bigl(H^a(b_F)(\alpha)\bigr)=DL\bigl(\chi_F(\alpha)\bigr)\circ d^{-1}.$$
All expressions are independent of $e,e',t$ and representatives; boundaries give zero derived morphisms and homotopic comparisons induce the same maps. No preservation of injective objects by $L$ is assumed.

These comparisons respect composition and coherent identifications of exact functors: for a second exact functor $L_2:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ with analogous data $(P'',S'',d_2,\lambda_2)$, where $\mathcal C$ is abelian with enough injectives, the comparison for $L_2L$, $d_2\circ L_2d$ and $(\lambda_2L)\circ\lambda$ is the composite of the two derived comparisons. If two such composites are identified by a natural isomorphism of the exact functors and their underived $d$ and $\lambda$ agree under it, their derived comparisons and the displayed Hom formulas agree under the induced derived isomorphism.

proof.text: Write $Q$ for the relevant localizations, and omit their canonical termwise identifications. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], $L$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms and descends to $DL$, commuting with shifts through the stated termwise comparison. By [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective], $I,J$ are K-injective. The morphism $Q(e')Q(Le)^{-1}:Q(LI)\to QJ$ therefore lifts to a homotopy class of chain maps $t:LI\to J$ by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Its composite with $Le$ has image $Q(e')$; injectivity of the localization map into the K-injective target $J$ gives $tLe\simeq e'$. The same argument gives uniqueness up to homotopy. Such resolutions are available: [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] gives an injective representative $QI\cong QF$, and the inverse isomorphism lifts to $e:F\to I$ by the same Hom bijection; $e$ is a quasi-isomorphism because its image under every cohomology functor is an isomorphism. Apply this also to $LF$. No injectivity of $LI$ has been used.

Let $u_K:Q(S(K))\to RS(QK)$ and $u'_T:Q(S'(T))\to RS'(QT)$ be the derived units supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective]. Its Kan factorization property applied to the natural maps $u'_{LK}Q(\lambda_K)$ gives the unique natural transformation $b$ satisfying $b_{QK}u_K=u'_{LK}Q(\lambda_K)$. The units $u_I,u'_J$ are isomorphisms by that node's injective-computation clause. Thus $c_e=RS(Qe)^{-1}u_I$ and $c'_{e'}=RS'(Qe')^{-1}u'_J$ identify $Q(SI),Q(S'J)$ with $RS(QF),RS'(Q(LF))$, respectively. The functors send the inverted arrows to isomorphisms because $e,e'$ are quasi-isomorphisms.

source.place: Tags 05TI (lemma-enough-injectives-right-derived), 05TH (lemma-injective-acyclic); Kan characterization as stated in lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective.

proof.text:
Naturality of $b$ at $Qe$, its defining factorization at $I$, and naturality of $u'$ at $t$ give
$$b_{QF}c_e=RS'(QLe)^{-1}u'_{LI}Q(\lambda_I),\qquad u'_JQ(S't)=RS'(Qt)u'_{LI}.$$
Since $Qt\,QLe=Qe'$, substitution gives
$$b_{QF}c_e=RS'(Qe')^{-1}u'_JQ(S't)Q(\lambda_I)=c'_{e'}Q(S't\circ\lambda_I).$$
This is the required injective-model formula. Every inverse here is the image of a quasi-isomorphism or a derived unit at an injective complex; $u'_{LI}$ is never inverted.

source.place: Tags 05TH and 05TI; explicit naturality calculation using the units from lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective.

proof.text:
For a cocycle $f:P\to I^a$, the hypothesis and naturality of $\theta'$ at $t^a$ yield
$$S'(t^a)\lambda_{I^a}\theta_{I^a}(f)=S'(t^a)\theta'_{LI^a}(Lf\,d^{-1})=\theta'_{J^a}(t^aLf\,d^{-1}).$$
The right-hand morphism is closed: $\partial_J^a t^a Lf\,d^{-1}=t^{a+1}L(\partial_I^a f)d^{-1}=0$. Naturality of $\theta$ with respect to the differentials identifies the complex $S(I)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(P,I^\bullet)$; likewise for $\theta'$ and $J$. Thus this equality of cocycles computes the map on their cohomology. Applying the Kan property to $\theta,\theta^{-1}$ gives mutually inverse derived transformations, since both composites factor the identity unit. Hence these are exactly the derived-$\theta$ identifications in the definition of $\chi,\chi'$.

source.place: Tags 05TH and 05TI; agent calculation from the assumed representability square and Kan uniqueness.

proof.text:
Let $\widetilde f:P[0]\to I[a]$ be the chain map of the cocycle. By [lem-sc-p1-rhom-hom-derived-roof], its class, transported by $c_e$ and $\theta$, has image $Q(e)[a]^{-1}Q(\widetilde f)$ under $\chi$. Steps 3--4 and the same roof formula for $J$ give image
$$Q(e')[a]^{-1}Q(t)[a]Q(L\widetilde f)d^{-1}$$
under $\chi'$ after applying $H^a(b)$. The equality $Qt\,QLe=Qe'$ implies $Q(e')[a]^{-1}Q(t)[a]=Q(Le)[a]^{-1}$. By the shift-normalized factorization in [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], the last display is therefore
$$DL\bigl(Q(e)[a]^{-1}Q(\widetilde f)\bigr)d^{-1}.$$
Here $d^{-1}$ denotes the map on complexes concentrated in degree zero, and all shifted factors use the termwise comparison fixed in the statement. Every cohomology class of $S(I)$ has a cocycle representative, so the asserted equation holds for every $\alpha$ and every integer $a$.

source.place: Tag 070I and the roof normalization of lem-sc-p1-rhom-hom-derived-roof; Tag 015F and shift comparison of lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization.

proof.text: If $f=\partial_I^{a-1}g$, the degree-$a-1$ map $(-1)^ag$ gives a chain homotopy from $\widetilde f$ to zero: the only nonzero source term is $P$ in degree zero, so the homotopy equation in that degree is $(-1)^a\partial_I^{a-1}((-1)^ag)=f$. Thus its localized map and its roof are zero. Additive functors carry a homotopy $h$ to the homotopy obtained by applying the functor to each $h^n$; in particular homotopic $t$ give the same map of cohomology. Finally step 3 identifies every resolution-based representative with the single canonical $b_{QF}$, and [lem-sc-p1-rhom-hom-derived-roof] supplies its normalized formula for every chosen resolution. Consequently changing $e,e',t$ or a cocycle representative changes neither the derived map nor the Hom formula.

source.place: Localization through the homotopy category (Tag 05RU); Tags 05TH, 05TI; resolution-uniform roof formula in lem-sc-p1-rhom-hom-derived-roof.

proof.text:
For the second datum write $b_2:RS'\to RS''DL_2$ and $u''$ for the third derived unit. At a bounded-below complex $K$, the defining equations give
$$ (b_{2,DL(QK)}b_{QK})u_K=b_{2,Q(LK)}u'_{LK}Q(\lambda_K)=u''_{L_2LK}Q(\lambda_{2,LK})Q(\lambda_K).$$
This is precisely the factorization equation for $\lambda_{\mathrm{tot}}=(\lambda_2L)\lambda$. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] identifies the composite with $b_{\mathrm{tot}}$, under the canonical identification $D(L_2L)=DL_2DL$. This identification is induced by the degreewise identity $L_2(LK)=(L_2L)K$ through localization. Moreover, applying the two assumed representability squares successively gives
$$\theta''_{L_2LM}\bigl(L_2Lf\,(d_2L_2d)^{-1}\bigr)=\lambda_{2,LM}\lambda_M\theta_M(f),$$
since $(d_2L_2d)^{-1}=(L_2d)^{-1}d_2^{-1}$. Thus the composite datum satisfies the hypotheses. Applying the already proved Hom formula twice gives $DL_2DL(\chi(\alpha))(L_2d)^{-1}d_2^{-1}$, which is exactly the formula for this composite datum.

source.place: Tags 05TI and 015F; explicit Kan-uniqueness and inverse-composition calculations.

proof.text:
For the final coherence assertion, put $E=L_2L$ and let $\zeta:E\xrightarrow{\sim}T$ be the given identification with another composite. The hypothesis means $\lambda_T=S''(\zeta)\lambda_E$ and $d_T\zeta_P=d_E$. The degreewise maps $\zeta_{K^n}$ form an isomorphism of complexes, natural in $K$ and compatible with shifts. Localizing it gives $D\zeta:DE\cong DT$; naturality first on chain maps and then on inverses of quasi-isomorphisms proves naturality on roofs. Naturality of the target derived unit gives
$$RS''(Q\zeta_K)b_{E,QK}u_K=RS''(Q\zeta_K)u''_{EK}Q\lambda_{E,K}=u''_{TK}Q\lambda_{T,K}.$$
Kan uniqueness therefore yields $RS''(D\zeta)b_E=b_T$. On Hom groups, naturality of $D\zeta$ at $\chi(\alpha):P[0]\to F[a]$ gives
$$D\zeta_F[a]\,DE(\chi(\alpha))d_E^{-1}=DT(\chi(\alpha))\zeta_Pd_E^{-1}=DT(\chi(\alpha))d_T^{-1}.$$
The source identity uses $d_T\zeta_P=d_E$. This proves agreement of the derived comparisons and their Hom formulas under the specified coherent identifications.
